summary: Expiry touches the ShortUrl entity (new nullable column), the create contract and validation, the cached value on the redirect hot path, and the redirect/metadata responses. Analytics, code generation and the repository are unaffected.

files.change: Add nullable ExpiresAt (DateTimeOffset?) and an IsExpired(now) helper.
CreateUrlRequest.ExpiresInMinutes, UrlResponse.ExpiresAt, ResolveStatus/ResolveResult for the redirect path, CachedLink cache value.
Set ExpiresAt on create; ResolveAsync returns Found/Expired/NotFound and checks expiry on cache hits; cache stores target + expiry.
Redirect returns 410 Gone for expired links (no click recorded); responses include expiresAt.

risks: Cached entries created before this change hold only the target URL; the cache value type changes, so old entries must not be read as the new type (in-memory cache is empty after deploy; Redis would need a key-version bump).
Schema change on short_urls (new nullable column): development SQLite is recreated automatically; a production database needs an EF migration.
A cached link must not outlive its expiry: expiry has to be evaluated on every request, not only on cache misses.
